small_guidance:
- Increase BLOCK_P (try 256/512) and tune num_warps (8) / num_stages (2-3) via triton.autotune; current 128/4 leaves the inner static_range loops (IC*KH*KW*POOL*POOL = 8*3*3*16 = 1152 iters) latency-bound per program.
- Replace the per-(dy,dx) reload of x with a single load of a (POOL+KH-1)×(POOL+KW-1) tile per (ic,oc,output-tile) and reuse it across the 9 kernel taps and 16 pool offsets — this cuts x-loads by ~16×.
- Avoid the global atomic_add into out[n] by accumulating per (n, oc, p-tile) into a [N, OC] buffer and doing a final small sum over OC on the host (or a second tiny kernel); the atomics on a length-128 vector serialize all OC*P_tiles writers.
large_guidance:
- Restructure as an im2col-style GEMM: tile (N, OC_BLOCK, OutSpatial_BLOCK) with K-loop over IC*KH*KW using tl.dot. Fuse the AvgPool window sum directly on the GEMM accumulator (each output-spatial tile represents pooled positions; accumulate POOL*POOL conv outputs into one pooled value in registers), then apply sigmoid and a warp/block reduce to sum over (OC, PH, PW) before a single atomic_add per program into out[n].
- Use channels-last (NHWC) input + weight layout so the K=IC*KH*KW reduction is contiguous; this enables tl.dot on (BLOCK_M=pooled-spatial, BLOCK_N=OC_tile, BLOCK_K=32/64) and saturates tensor-core-free FMA throughput on Ada.
- Make the kernel persistent per (n, oc_tile): loop over pooled-spatial tiles inside one program, keeping the OC_tile of weights resident in registers/SRAM across many spatial tiles — weight reuse is the dominant bandwidth win since OC=64, KH=KW=3, IC=8 (only 4.5KB of weights per oc_tile).
